BiblicalUsage: zânâb means the tail (literally or figuratively). In Exodus 4:4 we read, "And the LORD said unto Moses, Put forth thine hand, and take it by the tail." It appears again in Deuteronomy 28:13: "And the LORD shall make thee the head, and not the tail; and thou shalt be above only, and thou shalt not be beneath..."
TheologicalSignificance: zanab is the tail (literally or figuratively), and what strikes me is how much meaning God packs into a single word.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
